data.exact_reserve_text: The total gross claims reserves including prior years is $1,049m and the net total is $222m. During 2024, gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2022 and prior) increased by $99.5m. This was primarily due to poor experience and reserve strengthening in Syndicate 1919's Casualty Division in respect of the US business. On a net basis ultimate claims have increased by $21.3m. On 2020 and prior this gross experience in Casualty is net nil, due to the loss portfolio transfer on the 2020 & prior years of account. However, as there was IBNR strengthening on the 2021 and post underwriting years, these years have seen a net impact.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims reserves at the opening of 2024 were $1,016.525m. During 2024 the Syndicate recorded an adverse prioryear development of $99.5m (gross), driven primarily by poor experience and reserve strengthening in the Casualty division (US business) and by IBNR strengthening on 2021 and later underwriting years. This resulted in a net increase in ultimate claims of $21.3m after reinsurance. The movement is therefore an overall prioryear strengthening concentrated in Casualty.

data.data_quality_notes: All monetary amounts are reported in the report's native currency USD. The prior year gross movement ($99.5m) is taken verbatim from the managing agent's narrative (explicit gross figure). The report does not quantify the PYD by individual LOB other than stating it was primarily due to Casualty (US); therefore per-LOB PYD amounts are not provided. Claims development triangle is present (gross amounts in thousands) and was used for cross-checking.
